topLevel.why: Y's 19 parts follow the novel's real movements: front matter, New Bedford, chapel, Nantucket, sailing, the mates, the typhoon, the Rachel and the chase. X's parts are few and badly drawn: part 2 runs from Chapter 2 to mid-Chapter 29, part 3 is a 30-block sliver whose gist describes the Quarter-Deck oath it does not contain, and part 4 swallows Chapters 32–86, cetology and narrative alike.

gists.why: X's gists match their passages in every case and are specific. In four of the eight passages Y gives a gist about some other chapter (Pip, the try-works, the hat), which would mislead a reader.

weldedParts.why: Welds the New Bedford inn and chapel chapters to Nantucket, signing aboard the Pequod, the departure, the profiles of the mates and Ahab's first appearance (Ch. 2–29).
Welds the cetology digressions to major narrative chapters: the Quarter-Deck oath, 'Moby Dick', 'The Whiteness of the Whale', the first lowering, the Town-Ho's story and several gams (Ch. 32–86).
Joins the cetology classification to the Quarter-Deck oath and the dramatic chapters that follow it.

weldedParts.part: Try-works, omens, and the doubloon's many readings
weldedParts.why: Spans Ch. 79–105, covering head anatomy, the Grand Armada, several gams and the whale-skeleton chapters, yet its gist claims the quadrant smashing from Ch. 118.

inventedClaims.what: Gist describes Pip's abandonment; the passage is Ishmael's mast-head trance before Stubb's kill.
Gist describes Pip's abandonment; the passage is Fleece preaching to the sharks.
Gist describes the try-works and a near-disaster at the helm; the passage is about whalemen's abundant lamp oil.
Gist describes Pip in Ahab's cabin and the lost hat; the passage is Stubb's aside during the Rachel gam.

overall.why: This is a narrow call. Y's division into parts is far more usable as a map of the book, while X's top level collapses most of the novel into two oversized, mixed parts. Y's misplaced section gists are a serious flaw, but they matter less than X's broken overall structure.
